picks.name: holocloth
picks.licenseEvidence: LICENSE file: 'MIT License \u2014 Copyright (c) 2026 Dmitry Kurash ... Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy of this software...'
picks.gives: Custom GLSL iridescent/holographic foil shader with sparkle/glitter and bump-map handling, written directly against Three.js WebGL2 + React + TS — use as reference source (extract shader chunks) for the T50 foil-portrait effect.
picks.where: Port the fragment shader (fresnel + rainbow diffraction + sparkle noise) into OASIS's own ShaderMaterial for the T50 card foil layer.
picks.risk: Very new repo (4 commits, 2 months old) with no releases/tags to pin beyond commit SHA; treat as a study/reference, re-review the shader math before adopting verbatim; repo includes cloth-physics code not needed for OASIS (extract only the shader).

picks.name: guillocheJS
picks.licenseEvidence: LICENSE file: 'MIT License. Copyright (c) 2017 Guillaume Bonnet ... permission is hereby granted...'
picks.gives: Dependency-free vanilla-JS Canvas generator for hypotrochoid/epitrochoid/hypocycloid guilloche curves with HiDPI + PNG export — exactly the engraved gold-border pattern technique needed for T50.
picks.where: Run offline at build time (or once at runtime) to bake a guilloche PNG/canvas texture, then map it onto the card border geometry/material in Three.js.
picks.risk: Repo size ~36KB, no formal npm package or tags — vendor the ~500-line JS file directly and pin by commit SHA; no build tooling to verify beyond manual read.

picks.name: vanilla-tilt.js
picks.licenseEvidence: LICENSE file: 'MIT License \u2014 Copyright (c) 2017 \u0218andor Sergiu ... Permission is hereby granted, free of charge...'
picks.gives: Zero-dependency pointer-driven 3D tilt + glare micro-library (~6.8KB minified) for the card tilt/drag/flip and pointer-light-sweep interaction on the DOM-layer card face.
picks.where: Wrap as the pointer/tilt input driver for the T50 card container, feeding its computed tilt angles into the WebGL shader uniforms for the specular sweep.
picks.risk: No commits since Nov 2023 (outside the 12-month freshness preference) — stable/tiny/widely-used so low churn risk, but confirm it still behaves correctly under Tauri's WebKit/WebView2 pointer events before relying on it long-term; easy to fork given its size if abandoned.

rejected.name: pokemon-cards-css (simeydotme)
rejected.reason: LICENSE file is GPLv3 (verified directly), not MIT as often assumed from its popularity/badges — disallowed license for OASIS.

rejected.name: daniel-ilett/shaders-holo-card
rejected.reason: Unity/HLSL shader project, not Three.js/WebGL — wrong stack for a drop-in pick; would require a full rewrite rather than porting, so not scouted as a license-verified pick.

rejected.name: react-flip-tilt
rejected.reason: MIT but effectively unmaintained (last push 2023-11-07, only 1 star) and pulls in Framer Motion as a hard dependency, adding weight against the low-idle-CPU/offline-bundle constraints; vanilla-tilt.js covers the same need with zero dependencies.

top: Use holocloth's Three.js/WebGL2 shader source as a reference for the T50 foil+sparkle fragment shader (MIT, very active, but pin by commit and vet the math yourself).
Use guillocheJS to bake the engraved gold guilloche border as a texture offline (MIT, active, dependency-free, tiny).
Use vanilla-tilt.js to drive the pointer-based tilt/glare interaction on the card (MIT, tiny, ubiquitous, though its last commit is ~2.5 years old).
goal: Holo/foil trading-card shaders and techniques for T50 (iridescent foil, glitter, engraved/guilloche gold border, pointer-driven specular sweep, card tilt/flip) usable in Three.js or WebGL
